messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: April 30, 2020
Date of Discharge: May 21, 2020

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the GHESKIO MDR-TB hospital on April 30, 2020, with persistent fever, cough, and weight loss. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 and transferred to a separate building to prevent the spread of the virus. The patient did not require oxygen therapy and recovered from COVID-19 three weeks following diagnosis. He was continued on antituberculous therapy without complication.

Medical History:
The patient presented with a history of chronic cough, fever, and weight loss. He was evaluated by the medical staff with a physical examination, chest radiograph, and sputum analysis. The chest radiograph demonstrated a large right upper lobe cavity, with right middle lobe opacity and right hilar fullness. The GeneXpert sputum test was positive for the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with probable resistance to rifampin. The patient was lost to follow-up before hospitalization and initiation of therapy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up:
The patient is advised to continue regular follow-up with his healthcare provider. He is instructed to complete the prescribed antituberculous therapy and to maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in stable condition. He was advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider and to continue antituberculous therapy as prescribed.

Discharge Medications:
Antituberculous regimen composed of bedaquiline, levofloxacin, linezolid, clofazimine, and pyrazinimide was initiated and continued throughout hospitalization.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider. He should continue the prescribed antituberculous therapy and maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Pulmonary tuberculosis with probable rifampicin resistance (MDR-TB) is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, as shown by the cavitary lung lesion, the positive GeneXpert sputum test, and the antituberculous regimen. It belongs to chapter A (certain infectious and parasitic diseases), and respiratory tuberculosis confirmed bacteriologically is category A15. COVID-19 was an incidental comorbidity that did not change the principal diagnosis.

CODE: A15
